# Review pack: Yahya

**Status: DRAFT, unreviewed, unpublished.** Generated from `content/stories/yahya.draft.json`; do not edit this file (regenerate it).

Quran text: Tanzil Project (https://tanzil.net/), Uthmani 1.1, CC BY 3.0, reproduced verbatim. The English is the drafter's own wording of what the ayat state; it is not a translation of the Quran.

Notes from the drafter: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. The chapters are a reading order built from the ayat, not a chronology the Quran claims; surah order is not time order. The glad tidings are told in Zakariyya's account too; this draft states only what concerns Yahya. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on Yahya and his death. None is used in this draft.
- The words hasur (3:39), sayyid, hanan and zakah (19:13), the sense of the word for namesake (19:7), and judgment as a child (19:12) are left open; a scholar should decide how the page words each.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the word from God in 3:39 with a person, and accounts of Yahya's life and death. None is used in the story texts.
- The Quran gives the glad tidings of Yahya, his description, and the peace upon him; it does not give a story of his life, so the chapters are short.
- Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The good news of Yahya  (`#the-good-news`)

Cited ayat: 3:39, 19:7

> **3:39** فَنَادَتْهُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَهُوَ قَآئِمٌ يُصَلِّى فِى ٱلْمِحْرَابِ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ بِيَحْيَىٰ مُصَدِّقًۢا بِكَلِمَةٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَسَيِّدًا وَحَصُورًا وَنَبِيًّا مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

> **19:7** يَٰزَكَرِيَّآ إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَٰمٍ ٱسْمُهُۥ يَحْيَىٰ لَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيًّا

### Claims

**c1** (3:39): The angels called to Zakariyya while he stood praying in the mihrab that God gives him good news of Yahya, confirming a word from God, a leader, one who holds back, and a prophet from among the righteous.

**c2** (19:7): God told Zakariyya of a boy whose name is Yahya, for whom He had not made a namesake before.

### One-minute summary

Zakariyya was given good news of Yahya, a boy with that name for whom God had made no namesake before, a leader and a prophet from among the righteous [c1][c2].

### Complete story

The angels called to Zakariyya while he stood praying in the mihrab that God gives him good news of Yahya, confirming a word from God, a leader, one who holds back, and a prophet from among the righteous [c1]. God told Zakariyya of a boy whose name is Yahya, for whom He had not made a namesake before [c2].

### Deep study

The good news in 3:39 describes Yahya in a series of ways: as confirming a word from God, a leader, one who holds back, and a prophet from among the righteous [c1]. The good news in 19:7 gives his name and says that the name had no namesake before [c2]. The ayat do not say whether this is the same moment [c1][c2].

### Kids mode

Zakariyya was told that he would have a boy named Yahya [c1][c2]. Yahya would be a leader and a prophet from among the righteous [c1].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The good news gives the name first and the qualities after it [c1][c2]. A reader may notice that being a prophet is joined with being from among the righteous [c1].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: the sense of the Arabic hasur, one who holds back, or of sayyid, a leader; the ayah gives the words and the reviewer decides the wording.
- Not established: what the word from God is; the ayah says only that Yahya confirms it.
- Not established: the sense of the word for namesake, which can also read as equal; the reviewer decides the wording.
- Not established: Yahya's birth, parents' ages or the place of his birth beyond what the ayat of Zakariyya's account say.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: an identification of the word from God with a person; it is not used in the story texts.

## 2. Take the Book  (`#take-the-book`)

Cited ayat: 19:12-15

> **19:12** يَٰيَحْيَىٰ خُذِ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ بِقُوَّةٍ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ ٱلْحُكْمَ صَبِيًّا
>
> **19:13** وَحَنَانًا مِّن لَّدُنَّا وَزَكَوٰةً وَكَانَ تَقِيًّا
>
> **19:14** وَبَرًّۢا بِوَٰلِدَيْهِ وَلَمْ يَكُن جَبَّارًا عَصِيًّا
>
> **19:15** وَسَلَٰمٌ عَلَيْهِ يَوْمَ وُلِدَ وَيَوْمَ يَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ يُبْعَثُ حَيًّا

### Claims

**c1** (19:12): Yahya was told to take the Book with strength, and God gave him judgment as a child.

**c2** (19:13): God gave him tenderness from Himself, and purity, and he was one who feared God.

**c3** (19:14): He was dutiful to his parents, and was not a tyrant or disobedient.

**c4** (19:15): Peace is on him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive.

### One-minute summary

Yahya was told to take the Book with strength; God gave him judgment, tenderness and purity, he feared God and was dutiful to his parents, and peace is on him [c1][c2][c3][c4].

### Complete story

Yahya was told to take the Book with strength, and God gave him judgment as a child [c1]. God gave him tenderness from Himself, and purity, and he was one who feared God [c2]. He was dutiful to his parents, and was not a tyrant or disobedient [c3]. Peace is on him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive [c4].

### Deep study

The first words are a command addressed to him by name [c1]. The following ayat describe him as a description, by what God gave him and by what he was [c2][c3]. The last ayah is a statement of peace on the day of his birth, the day of his death and the day he is raised [c4]. The words tenderness (hanan) and purity (zakah) are given without further explanation [c2].

### Kids mode

Yahya was told to hold on firmly to the Book [c1]. He was kind to his parents and was not harsh [c3]. Peace is on him [c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The description joins duty to God with duty to parents [c2][c3]. A reader may notice that the ayat on Yahya end with peace upon him on the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: which Book Yahya was told to take, or what it contained; the ayah says only the Book.
- Not established: what judgment as a child consisted of, or how old he was; the ayah says child and no more.
- Not established: the exact senses of hanan (tenderness) and zakah (purity) here; the reviewer decides the wording.
- Not established: how he died, or when; the ayah says only the day he dies.
- Not established: whether the peace on him is a greeting or a statement; the ayah has the word alone.

## 3. Given, and named among the righteous  (`#named-among-the-righteous`)

Cited ayat: 6:85, 21:90

> **6:85** وَزَكَرِيَّا وَيَحْيَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ وَإِلْيَاسَ كُلٌّ مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

> **21:90** فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥ يَحْيَىٰ وَأَصْلَحْنَا لَهُۥ زَوْجَهُۥٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ يُسَٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَيَدْعُونَنَا رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا وَكَانُوا۟ لَنَا خَٰشِعِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (21:90): God answered Zakariyya, gave him Yahya, and put his wife right for him.

**c2** (21:90): The ayah says of them that they used to hasten to good deeds, call on God in hope and in fear, and were humble before Him.

**c3** (6:85): Yahya is named, with Zakariyya and others, each described as being among the righteous.

### One-minute summary

God gave Yahya to Zakariyya in answer to his call, and Yahya is named among those each described as righteous [c1][c3].

### Complete story

God answered Zakariyya, gave him Yahya, and put his wife right for him [c1]. The ayah says of them that they used to hasten to good deeds, call on God in hope and in fear, and were humble before Him [c2]. Yahya is named, with Zakariyya and others, each described as being among the righteous [c3].

### Deep study

The ayah on the gift of Yahya is brief and speaks of the answer to Zakariyya's call [c1]. The description that follows is in the plural and does not say who is included [c2]. In 6:85 Yahya is named in a list, and each in the list is described as righteous [c3].

### Kids mode

God answered Zakariyya and gave him Yahya [c1]. Yahya is named among the righteous [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): Yahya is spoken of first as a gift from God and then as one of the righteous [c1][c3]. The ayah describes those it speaks of as hastening to good deeds and humble before God [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who they are in 21:90, whether Zakariyya, his wife and Yahya or others; the plural is not explained.
- Not established: what put his wife right means, or whether it refers to her barrenness.
- Not established: why the others named in 6:85 are listed with Yahya; this draft states only the part that concerns Yahya and Zakariyya.
